thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 502/5xx rates observed from ALB 'inference-api-alb' serving inference-api in us-west-2. Spike started ~5m ago. Impact: ~18-25% errors for users routed to us-west-2b. Auto-escalation -> paging oncall-sre.

sam: I'm on it. Paging in. Checking target health and recent deploys.

jess: no deploys in the last hour from infra. I see a bunch of target deregistrations in the last ~3m from us-west-2b. Possible instance churn.

sam: running quick checks:
```
# target health
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:111:targetgroup/inference-tg/abcd1234 
# ASG size
aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names inference-api-asg
```

sam: describe-target-health shows ~60% targets Unhealthy in us-west-2b, 0/8 healthy. 2xx responses from other AZs.

jess: CloudTrail shows repeated EBS detach events for instances in us-west-2b starting ~6m ago. Looks like a storage flapping issue: `DetachVolume` events followed by instance reboots.

lia: customer impact? Any major customers seeing errors or just background jobs?

support: initial telemetry from Sentry/ingestion: top customers in us-west-2 see elevated latency and 502s; some timeouts upstream are bubbling as 502s at the ALB. Churn seems concentrated to a subset of instances (same AZ). No PII leaked.

ops-lead: immediate mitigation: reduce traffic routed to us-west-2b. Two options: 1) adjust Route53 weighted routing to shift traffic to us-west-2a/c (fast, DNS TTL 30s), 2) increase ASG to spin replacement instances and cordon unhealthy ones. Do both in parallel.

sam: agree. I'll push a Route53 weight change now to move ~75% away from us-west-2b while we rebuild.

jess: I'll start a force-replace of the affected instances in the ASG and temporarily increase desired capacity by +4 to avoid capacity dip. Commands:
```
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name inference-api-asg --desired-capacity 14 --honor-cooldown
for i in $(aws ec2 describe-instances --filters \"Name=availability-zone,Values=us-west-2b\" \"Name=tag:Role,Values=inference-api\" --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId' --output text); do 
  aws ec2 reboot-instances --instance-ids $i || true
done
```

pagerduty-bot: Incident: P1 - inference-api 5xx spike in us-west-2. Major incident call suggested.

support: Draft status update for status.redwood.ai: 
\"Redwood Status: Degraded performance for inference API in us-west-2. Engineers are investigating elevated 5xx rates affecting a subset of capacity in us-west-2b. We are mitigating by shifting traffic and replacing impacted instances. More updates in 15 minutes.\"

ops-lead: good. Post that now. Lia, can you craft the customer-facing blurb for our top 20 customers? Mention mitigation and ETA (15-30m).

lia: on it. Short message ready. Will DM top accounts and post to status page.

sam: Route53 weight change pushed. Confirming propagation (TTL 30). Monitoring error rate.

jess: new instances booting in us-west-2b, but CloudWatch shows EBS attach failures for a subset. Could be EBS API throttling or underlying AZ EBS congestion. I'm escalating to cloud provider via support channel.

sam: Observed logs on the ALB for 502s: backend returned \"socket hang up\" / \"ECONNRESET\" from a few instances prior to detaches.

support: Collecting request IDs for impacted customers to provide to SREs and for post-incident communication.

ops-lead: If EBS API is degraded in the AZ, replacing instances won't help until attach succeeds. Plan B: serve more traffic from us-west-2a/c and reduce reliance on 2b. Keep ASG min capacity the same to avoid more churn.

jess: Confirmed via AWS health dashboard (partial) — there are elevated EBS API error rates in a subset of us-west-2. I've opened a ticket with AWS support (case #CASE-987654). Waiting on response.

sam: Roll-forward mitigation complete: current traffic split approx 80% away from us-west-2b. Error rate for overall region down from 22% -> 6% in last 3m. Monitoring for regressions.

lia: Notifying customers and posting update. Support is tracking customers with SLO/paid SLAs to escalate to account teams.

pagerduty-bot: Major incident bridge started: https://call.redwood.ai/bridges/1719234567 (bridges auto-created).

support: Internal note: impact window currently ~5-25 minutes depending on DNS TTL. Some customers on sticky sessions might still hit affected instances for a short window.

alex: I'm taking the on-call handoff for the next 2 hours to monitor remediation progress and coordinate with AWS. Tag me for any escalations.

sam: handing off to alex. I've collected logs and runbooks in the incident channel thread. Running a short healthcheck script against ALBs and TGs every 30s.

ops-lead: assign postmortem owner: jess. Include: timeline, root cause (EBS attach/API errors in us-west-2b), why instance churn occurred, why Route53 weight/ALB didn't auto-shift fully earlier, and recommendations (retry/backoff changes on attach, cross-AZ capacity buffer, longer DNS TTL planning).

jess: will own postmortem. Drafting RCA template now.

sam: current status: region error rate stabilized at ~4-7%, us-west-2b still shows degraded capacity but not service-wide failure. AWS acknowledged elevated EBS API errors and provided mitigation ETA ~2-3 hours for full recovery; they're offering targeted support and follow-up.

lia: I've alerted sales for impacted enterprise customers and scheduled 1:1s where SLA credits might be requested.

ops-lead: good work. Keep the channel updated with any AWS updates. We'll convert to a formal incident doc for the ops wiki after the bridge.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> status: mitigating. Updated tags: network/storage, region: us-west-2, owner: jess.

alex: I'll keep monitoring and will escalate to the escalation chain if error rate creeps >10% region-wide. Handoff complete to alex for active monitoring.

support: final customer update posted to status.redwood.ai and sent to top accounts. Will append a follow-up once postmortem is ready.

jess: capturing all artifacts and will schedule the postmortem meeting tomorrow.

sam: closing on-call tasks here — moving to watchlist. If anything flares, ping oncall (alex) or page again.

ops-lead: incident status at handoff: MITIGATED (partial). Impact reduced via DNS traffic shift; underlying provider EBS issue remains active. Next steps: postmortem, follow-up with AWS on root cause, and update runbooks to include quicker cross-AZ traffic shifting instructions.

incident-bot: Incident thread archived for record.\"
